A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). ## OpenPets

OpenPets MCP tools may be available.

Use OpenPets as a short visible status channel for meaningful coding progress:
- Use `openpets_say` when starting, completing, blocking, or needing review on non-trivial work.
- Keep messages brief, user-facing, and non-sensitive.
- Do not include code, logs, secrets, URLs, or file paths.
- Use `openpets_react` for small visual or emotional feedback.
- Use `openpets_status` only when checking availability or the targeted pet.
- Do not spam every internal step.

# CLAUDE.md - Claude Code Extension for Visual Studio

## Project Overview

Visual Studio Extension (VSIX) for VS 2022/2026 — integrates AI code assistants (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor Agent, Open Code, Devin, PI, Google Antigravity, Reasonix, Qwen Code, and Grok) via a native chat tab driven by each CLI's headless protocol ("native mode", default since v179.0) or an embedded terminal (Win32 `SetParent` interop).

- Author: Daniel Carvalho Liedke | License: MIT
- Repository: https://github.com/dliedke/ClaudeCodeExtension
- Current Version: 290.0 | Target Framework: .NET Framework 4.7.2

Step-by-step procedures for recurring tasks (release, Exp-hive debugging, publish, adding a
provider/setting/UI file) live in `docs/SKILLS.md`. Short build/style brief for non-Claude agents: `docs/AGENTS.md`.

---

## MANDATORY: Version & Documentation Updates

Every development session that modifies code MUST update before finishing:

Versioning scheme (since 11.0): each release bumps the MAJOR version by one — 22.0 → 23.0 → 24.0 and so on. Always use `.0` as the minor (AssemblyVersion `24.0.0.0`, manifest `24.0`, README `### Version 24.0`). Do not resume 10.x-style minor bumps.

1. `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs`: Bump `AssemblyVersion` and `AssemblyFileVersion`
2. `source.extension.vsixmanifest`: Bump `Version` in `<Identity>` tag
3. `README.md`: Add `### Version X.Y` entry at top of `## Version History`
   - Style: Short, business-focused. One sentence per bullet (two max). Describe the user-visible feature or fix, not the implementation.
   - Avoid: code/file/class/method names, internal selectors, file paths, constants, line numbers, JS snippets, framework jargon (`CoreWebView2`, `INPUT_RECORD`, `NavigationCompleted`, etc.), step-by-step "how it works" explanations, and PR-description-style root-cause analysis.
   - Keep: what the user gets ("auto-confirms proxy block screens"), opt-in/opt-out status, and the menu/setting name they interact with.
   - Technical details belong in commit messages and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, not in release notes.
   - Merging a contributor PR: besides the "Thanks to [@login](https://github.com/login) for this release (#N)." line in the version entry, update the author's PR count in README's `## Thank You, Contributors` list (add a `1 PR` row for a first-time contributor). Keep the list sorted by PR count descending, ties alphabetical (case-insensitive); the owner `dliedke` is not listed. Counts include every PR the author opened (open, closed or merged) — recount with `gh pr list --state all --limit 1000 --json author`.
   - Other README sections (Features, Supported AI Providers, System Requirements, Settings & Menus, etc.): Edits MUST be minimal. Update only the exact line/bullet affected by the change. Do not rewrite paragraphs, expand explanations, add subsections, reorder content, or restructure tables. If a new provider/setting needs a row, add one row. If a feature description needs a word change, change the word. README is reference doc — keep it slim to avoid file bloat.

## Build & Test

```bash
# Release
'/c/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Enterprise/MSBuild/Current/Bin/MSBuild.exe' ClaudeCodeExtension.sln -p:Configuration=Release -v:minimal

# Debug
'/c/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Enterprise/MSBuild/Current/Bin/MSBuild.exe' ClaudeCodeExtension.sln -p:Configuration=Debug -v:minimal
```

- F5 / Ctrl+F5 in Visual Studio → experimental instance with `/rootsuffix Exp`, for Debug and Release

### Debugging in the Exp hive (`deploy-exp.cmd`)

The VSSDK targets default `DeployExtension` to false, so the csproj sets `VSSDKTargetPlatformRegRootSuffix=Exp` and turns `DeployExtension` on for any configuration built inside Visual Studio. Without those two properties F5 opens an Exp instance with no extension in it. Command-line builds (`test.cmd`, `publish.cmd`) keep the default and deploy nothing.

```bash
./deploy-exp.cmd            # build Debug + deploy to the Exp hive
./deploy-exp.cmd -release   # build Release instead of Debug
./deploy-exp.cmd -run       # the above, then start devenv /rootsuffix Exp with the solution
./deploy-exp.cmd -run -open <path.sln>   # start Exp with another solution (e.g. a demo app, so F5 debugs it)
```

- Close the Exp instance before deploying — otherwise it keeps running the previous build.
- A first deploy into a hive that never had the extension fails with `VSSDK1031 ... could not be found`; the script recovers by running `devenv /rootsuffix Exp /updateconfiguration` and retrying.
- The same VSSDK1031 (in VS or from the script) appears when an idle 32-bit MSBuild node from an earlier VS build still holds the Exp hive's `privateregistry.bin` open — `/updateconfiguration` then silently merges nothing. The script ends those nodes before each attempt; inside VS, kill the `MSBuild.exe ... /nodemode:2` process and rebuild.
- Each deploy lands in a version-named folder, so a version bump leaves the previous one behind and the hive can keep loading the older assembly with no error anywhere. The `RemoveStaleExpDeployments` target in the csproj deletes the sibling version folders after every deploy to prevent that.

### Tests (`test.cmd`)

```bash
./test.cmd    # build Tests/ + run the unit suite (seconds, no VS)
```

- Runs `Tests/ClaudeCodeExtension.Tests.csproj` under `vstest.console.exe`: version/package guards (the Newtonsoft pin that would have caught #112, version consistency across the three sources) plus unit tests of the pure helpers.
- `publish.cmd` calls `test.cmd` before the Release rebuild. `SKIP_TESTS=1` bypasses the gate.
- The test project is in the solution without a `Release|Any CPU.Build.0` entry, so the Release rebuild in `publish.cmd` does not build it.
- Everything that needs a running Visual Studio (terminal embedding, provider round-trip, settings dialog) is tested manually with F5.

### Publishing

When the user asks to publish the app (or any equivalent phrasing like "publish the extension", "publish to marketplace", "ship it"), run `publish.cmd` from the repo root. Do not invoke MSBuild or marketplace APIs manually — `publish.cmd` is the authoritative deployment automation.

`publish.cmd` performs: Clean → Rebuild Release → publish VSIX via `VsixPublisher.exe` with `publishManifest.json`. Falls back from VS 2026 to VS 2022 tool paths automatically. Uses `VsixPub0038` log marker to detect success (works around VsixPublisher telemetry crash in VS 18).

`publishManifest.json`: Marketplace metadata — publisher `dliedke`, category `coding`, free, Q&A enabled, README.md as overview.

## Architecture — Key Non-Obvious Details

Deep per-file gotchas and design decisions live in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (kept out of this
always-loaded file to keep context lean). Before editing any file below, read its section in that
doc — it captures non-obvious behavior that isn't apparent from the code:

Five cross-cutting rules (full text in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` → *Cross-Cutting Rules*) — read before touching provider selection, UI captions, terminal focus, anything that sends text to the agent, or a value chosen for performance:
- Active provider UI rule (v24.0): provider-dependent UI (checkmarks, captions, menu visibility, active labels) must use `_currentRunningProvider` when a terminal is alive, falling back to `_settings.SelectedProvider` only before launch.
- Terminal focus rule (v26.0): never focus the embedded terminal with direct `SetForegroundWindow`/`SetFocus`; use `FocusTerminalForInputAsync()`/`FocusTerminalForInput()`/`FocusTerminalWindow()`. Hook focus checks stay Win32-only.
- Agent send rule (v82.0): send agent-bound text through `SendTextToAgentAsync()`, not `SendTextToTerminalAsync()` — native mode has no console. Console-only traffic (slash commands, CLI updates, plugin installs) is the exception; new console-scraping logic must bail out when `IsNativeModeActive`.
- Chat localization rule (v269.0, whole extension since v270.0): new or changed UI text — chat, panel, menus, dialogs, message boxes — is wrapped in `L("...")`/`N("...")`/`{local:Loc '...'}` and translated in every `lang/*.json` in the same change (recipe: `docs/SKILLS.md` → *Localize chat text*); `test.cmd` fails on a missing or orphaned translation. Text set from code must also be redone by `RefreshChatLanguage()` (or a tool window's own `Loc.LanguageChanged` handler) so a language switch reaches everything already open.
- Performance values rule (v279.0): the resumed-transcript limits and any other value chosen for performance (throttle intervals, virtualization cache, rendering caps) change only together with a measurement recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` (method, machine, before/after); `ReplayLimitsMatchTheMeasuredValues` pins the limits.

# CLAUDE.md - Claude Code Extension for Visual Studio

## Project Overview

Visual Studio Extension (VSIX) for VS 2022/2026 — integrates AI code assistants (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor Agent, Open Code, Devin, PI, Google Antigravity, Reasonix, Qwen Code, and Grok) via a native chat tab driven by each CLI's headless protocol ("native mode", default since v179.0) or an embedded terminal (Win32 `SetParent` interop).

- Author: Daniel Carvalho Liedke | License: MIT
- Repository: https://github.com/dliedke/ClaudeCodeExtension
- Current Version: 290.0 | Target Framework: .NET Framework 4.7.2

Step-by-step procedures for recurring tasks (release, Exp-hive debugging, publish, adding a
provider/setting/UI file) live in `docs/SKILLS.md`. Short build/style brief for non-Claude agents: `docs/AGENTS.md`.

---

## MANDATORY: Version & Documentation Updates

Every development session that modifies code MUST update before finishing:

Versioning scheme (since 11.0): each release bumps the MAJOR version by one — 22.0 → 23.0 → 24.0 and so on. Always use `.0` as the minor (AssemblyVersion `24.0.0.0`, manifest `24.0`, README `### Version 24.0`). Do not resume 10.x-style minor bumps.

1. `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs`: Bump `AssemblyVersion` and `AssemblyFileVersion`
2. `source.extension.vsixmanifest`: Bump `Version` in `<Identity>` tag
3. `README.md`: Add `### Version X.Y` entry at top of `## Version History`
   - Style: Short, business-focused. One sentence per bullet (two max). Describe the user-visible feature or fix, not the implementation.
   - Avoid: code/file/class/method names, internal selectors, file paths, constants, line numbers, JS snippets, framework jargon (`CoreWebView2`, `INPUT_RECORD`, `NavigationCompleted`, etc.), step-by-step "how it works" explanations, and PR-description-style root-cause analysis.
   - Keep: what the user gets ("auto-confirms proxy block screens"), opt-in/opt-out status, and the menu/setting name they interact with.
   - Technical details belong in commit messages and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, not in release notes.
   - Merging a contributor PR: besides the "Thanks to [@login](https://github.com/login) for this release (#N)." line in the version entry, update the author's PR count in README's `## Thank You, Contributors` list (add a `1 PR` row for a first-time contributor). Keep the list sorted by PR count descending, ties alphabetical (case-insensitive); the owner `dliedke` is not listed. Counts include every PR the author opened (open, closed or merged) — recount with `gh pr list --state all --limit 1000 --json author`.
   - Other README sections (Features, Supported AI Providers, System Requirements, Settings & Menus, etc.): Edits MUST be minimal. Update only the exact line/bullet affected by the change. Do not rewrite paragraphs, expand explanations, add subsections, reorder content, or restructure tables. If a new provider/setting needs a row, add one row. If a feature description needs a word change, change the word. README is reference doc — keep it slim to avoid file bloat.

## Build & Test

```bash
# Release
'/c/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Enterprise/MSBuild/Current/Bin/MSBuild.exe' ClaudeCodeExtension.sln -p:Configuration=Release -v:minimal

# Debug
'/c/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Enterprise/MSBuild/Current/Bin/MSBuild.exe' ClaudeCodeExtension.sln -p:Configuration=Debug -v:minimal
```

- F5 / Ctrl+F5 in Visual Studio → experimental instance with `/rootsuffix Exp`, for Debug and Release

### Debugging in the Exp hive (`deploy-exp.cmd`)

The VSSDK targets default `DeployExtension` to false, so the csproj sets `VSSDKTargetPlatformRegRootSuffix=Exp` and turns `DeployExtension` on for any configuration built inside Visual Studio. Without those two properties F5 opens an Exp instance with no extension in it. Command-line builds (`test.cmd`, `publish.cmd`) keep the default and deploy nothing.

```bash
./deploy-exp.cmd            # build Debug + deploy to the Exp hive
./deploy-exp.cmd -release   # build Release instead of Debug
./deploy-exp.cmd -run       # the above, then start devenv /rootsuffix Exp with the solution
./deploy-exp.cmd -run -open <path.sln>   # start Exp with another solution (e.g. a demo app, so F5 debugs it)
```

- Close the Exp instance before deploying — otherwise it keeps running the previous build.
- A first deploy into a hive that never had the extension fails with `VSSDK1031 ... could not be found`; the script recovers by running `devenv /rootsuffix Exp /updateconfiguration` and retrying.
- The same VSSDK1031 (in VS or from the script) appears when an idle 32-bit MSBuild node from an earlier VS build still holds the Exp hive's `privateregistry.bin` open — `/updateconfiguration` then silently merges nothing. The script ends those nodes before each attempt; inside VS, kill the `MSBuild.exe ... /nodemode:2` process and rebuild.
- Each deploy lands in a version-named folder, so a version bump leaves the previous one behind and the hive can keep loading the older assembly with no error anywhere. The `RemoveStaleExpDeployments` target in the csproj deletes the sibling version folders after every deploy to prevent that.

### Tests (`test.cmd`)

```bash
./test.cmd    # build Tests/ + run the unit suite (seconds, no VS)
```

- Runs `Tests/ClaudeCodeExtension.Tests.csproj` under `vstest.console.exe`: version/package guards (the Newtonsoft pin that would have caught #112, version consistency across the three sources) plus unit tests of the pure helpers.
- `publish.cmd` calls `test.cmd` before the Release rebuild. `SKIP_TESTS=1` bypasses the gate.
- The test project is in the solution without a `Release|Any CPU.Build.0` entry, so the Release rebuild in `publish.cmd` does not build it.
- Everything that needs a running Visual Studio (terminal embedding, provider round-trip, settings dialog) is tested manually with F5.

### Publishing

When the user asks to publish the app (or any equivalent phrasing like "publish the extension", "publish to marketplace", "ship it"), run `publish.cmd` from the repo root. Do not invoke MSBuild or marketplace APIs manually — `publish.cmd` is the authoritative deployment automation.

`publish.cmd` performs: Clean → Rebuild Release → publish VSIX via `VsixPublisher.exe` with `publishManifest.json`. Falls back from VS 2026 to VS 2022 tool paths automatically. Uses `VsixPub0038` log marker to detect success (works around VsixPublisher telemetry crash in VS 18).

`publishManifest.json`: Marketplace metadata — publisher `dliedke`, category `coding`, free, Q&A enabled, README.md as overview.

## Architecture — Key Non-Obvious Details

Deep per-file gotchas and design decisions live in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (kept out of this
always-loaded file to keep context lean). Before editing any file below, read its section in that
doc — it captures non-obvious behavior that isn't apparent from the code:

Five cross-cutting rules (full text in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` → *Cross-Cutting Rules*) — read before touching provider selection, UI captions, terminal focus, anything that sends text to the agent, or a value chosen for performance:
- Active provider UI rule (v24.0): provider-dependent UI (checkmarks, captions, menu visibility, active labels) must use `_currentRunningProvider` when a terminal is alive, falling back to `_settings.SelectedProvider` only before launch.
- Terminal focus rule (v26.0): never focus the embedded terminal with direct `SetForegroundWindow`/`SetFocus`; use `FocusTerminalForInputAsync()`/`FocusTerminalForInput()`/`FocusTerminalWindow()`. Hook focus checks stay Win32-only.
- Agent send rule (v82.0): send agent-bound text through `SendTextToAgentAsync()`, not `SendTextToTerminalAsync()` — native mode has no console. Console-only traffic (slash commands, CLI updates, plugin installs) is the exception; new console-scraping logic must bail out when `IsNativeModeActive`.
- Chat localization rule (v269.0, whole extension since v270.0): new or changed UI text — chat, panel, menus, dialogs, message boxes — is wrapped in `L("...")`/`N("...")`/`{local:Loc '...'}` and translated in every `lang/*.json` in the same change (recipe: `docs/SKILLS.md` → *Localize chat text*); `test.cmd` fails on a missing or orphaned translation. Text set from code must also be redone by `RefreshChatLanguage()` (or a tool window's own `Loc.LanguageChanged` handler) so a language switch reaches everything already open.
- Performance values rule (v279.0): the resumed-transcript limits and any other value chosen for performance (throttle intervals, virtualization cache, rendering caps) change only together with a measurement recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` (method, machine, before/after); `ReplayLimitsMatchTheMeasuredValues` pins the limits.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000ms / 30 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.

- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.

- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

# CLAUDE.md - Claude Code Extension for Visual Studio

## Project Overview

Visual Studio Extension (VSIX) for VS 2022/2026 — integrates AI code assistants (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor Agent, Open Code, Devin, PI, Google Antigravity, Reasonix, Qwen Code, and Grok) via a native chat tab driven by each CLI's headless protocol ("native mode", default since v179.0) or an embedded terminal (Win32 `SetParent` interop).

- Author: Daniel Carvalho Liedke | License: MIT
- Repository: https://github.com/dliedke/ClaudeCodeExtension
- Current Version: 290.0 | Target Framework: .NET Framework 4.7.2

Step-by-step procedures for recurring tasks (release, Exp-hive debugging, publish, adding a
provider/setting/UI file) live in `docs/SKILLS.md`. Short build/style brief for non-Claude agents: `docs/AGENTS.md`.

---

## MANDATORY: Version & Documentation Updates

Every development session that modifies code MUST update before finishing:

Versioning scheme (since 11.0): each release bumps the MAJOR version by one — 22.0 → 23.0 → 24.0 and so on. Always use `.0` as the minor (AssemblyVersion `24.0.0.0`, manifest `24.0`, README `### Version 24.0`). Do not resume 10.x-style minor bumps.

1. `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs`: Bump `AssemblyVersion` and `AssemblyFileVersion`
2. `source.extension.vsixmanifest`: Bump `Version` in `<Identity>` tag
3. `README.md`: Add `### Version X.Y` entry at top of `## Version History`
   - Style: Short, business-focused. One sentence per bullet (two max). Describe the user-visible feature or fix, not the implementation.
   - Avoid: code/file/class/method names, internal selectors, file paths, constants, line numbers, JS snippets, framework jargon (`CoreWebView2`, `INPUT_RECORD`, `NavigationCompleted`, etc.), step-by-step "how it works" explanations, and PR-description-style root-cause analysis.
   - Keep: what the user gets ("auto-confirms proxy block screens"), opt-in/opt-out status, and the menu/setting name they interact with.
   - Technical details belong in commit messages and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, not in release notes.
   - Merging a contributor PR: besides the "Thanks to [@login](https://github.com/login) for this release (#N)." line in the version entry, update the author's PR count in README's `## Thank You, Contributors` list (add a `1 PR` row for a first-time contributor). Keep the list sorted by PR count descending, ties alphabetical (case-insensitive); the owner `dliedke` is not listed. Counts include every PR the author opened (open, closed or merged) — recount with `gh pr list --state all --limit 1000 --json author`.
   - Other README sections (Features, Supported AI Providers, System Requirements, Settings & Menus, etc.): Edits MUST be minimal. Update only the exact line/bullet affected by the change. Do not rewrite paragraphs, expand explanations, add subsections, reorder content, or restructure tables. If a new provider/setting needs a row, add one row. If a feature description needs a word change, change the word. README is reference doc — keep it slim to avoid file bloat.

## Build & Test

```bash
# Release
'/c/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Enterprise/MSBuild/Current/Bin/MSBuild.exe' ClaudeCodeExtension.sln -p:Configuration=Release -v:minimal

# Debug
'/c/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Enterprise/MSBuild/Current/Bin/MSBuild.exe' ClaudeCodeExtension.sln -p:Configuration=Debug -v:minimal
```

- F5 / Ctrl+F5 in Visual Studio → experimental instance with `/rootsuffix Exp`, for Debug and Release

### Debugging in the Exp hive (`deploy-exp.cmd`)

The VSSDK targets default `DeployExtension` to false, so the csproj sets `VSSDKTargetPlatformRegRootSuffix=Exp` and turns `DeployExtension` on for any configuration built inside Visual Studio. Without those two properties F5 opens an Exp instance with no extension in it. Command-line builds (`test.cmd`, `publish.cmd`) keep the default and deploy nothing.

```bash
./deploy-exp.cmd            # build Debug + deploy to the Exp hive
./deploy-exp.cmd -release   # build Release instead of Debug
./deploy-exp.cmd -run       # the above, then start devenv /rootsuffix Exp with the solution
./deploy-exp.cmd -run -open <path.sln>   # start Exp with another solution (e.g. a demo app, so F5 debugs it)
```

- Close the Exp instance before deploying — otherwise it keeps running the previous build.
- A first deploy into a hive that never had the extension fails with `VSSDK1031 ... could not be found`; the script recovers by running `devenv /rootsuffix Exp /updateconfiguration` and retrying.
- The same VSSDK1031 (in VS or from the script) appears when an idle 32-bit MSBuild node from an earlier VS build still holds the Exp hive's `privateregistry.bin` open — `/updateconfiguration` then silently merges nothing. The script ends those nodes before each attempt; inside VS, kill the `MSBuild.exe ... /nodemode:2` process and rebuild.
- Each deploy lands in a version-named folder, so a version bump leaves the previous one behind and the hive can keep loading the older assembly with no error anywhere. The `RemoveStaleExpDeployments` target in the csproj deletes the sibling version folders after every deploy to prevent that.

### Tests (`test.cmd`)

```bash
./test.cmd    # build Tests/ + run the unit suite (seconds, no VS)
```

- Runs `Tests/ClaudeCodeExtension.Tests.csproj` under `vstest.console.exe`: version/package guards (the Newtonsoft pin that would have caught #112, version consistency across the three sources) plus unit tests of the pure helpers.
- `publish.cmd` calls `test.cmd` before the Release rebuild. `SKIP_TESTS=1` bypasses the gate.
- The test project is in the solution without a `Release|Any CPU.Build.0` entry, so the Release rebuild in `publish.cmd` does not build it.
- Everything that needs a running Visual Studio (terminal embedding, provider round-trip, settings dialog) is tested manually with F5.

### Publishing

When the user asks to publish the app (or any equivalent phrasing like "publish the extension", "publish to marketplace", "ship it"), run `publish.cmd` from the repo root. Do not invoke MSBuild or marketplace APIs manually — `publish.cmd` is the authoritative deployment automation.

`publish.cmd` performs: Clean → Rebuild Release → publish VSIX via `VsixPublisher.exe` with `publishManifest.json`. Falls back from VS 2026 to VS 2022 tool paths automatically. Uses `VsixPub0038` log marker to detect success (works around VsixPublisher telemetry crash in VS 18).

`publishManifest.json`: Marketplace metadata — publisher `dliedke`, category `coding`, free, Q&A enabled, README.md as overview.

## Architecture — Key Non-Obvious Details

Deep per-file gotchas and design decisions live in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (kept out of this
always-loaded file to keep context lean). Before editing any file below, read its section in that
doc — it captures non-obvious behavior that isn't apparent from the code:

Five cross-cutting rules (full text in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` → *Cross-Cutting Rules*) — read before touching provider selection, UI captions, terminal focus, anything that sends text to the agent, or a value chosen for performance:
- Active provider UI rule (v24.0): provider-dependent UI (checkmarks, captions, menu visibility, active labels) must use `_currentRunningProvider` when a terminal is alive, falling back to `_settings.SelectedProvider` only before launch.
- Terminal focus rule (v26.0): never focus the embedded terminal with direct `SetForegroundWindow`/`SetFocus`; use `FocusTerminalForInputAsync()`/`FocusTerminalForInput()`/`FocusTerminalWindow()`. Hook focus checks stay Win32-only.
- Agent send rule (v82.0): send agent-bound text through `SendTextToAgentAsync()`, not `SendTextToTerminalAsync()` — native mode has no console. Console-only traffic (slash commands, CLI updates, plugin installs) is the exception; new console-scraping logic must bail out when `IsNativeModeActive`.
- Chat localization rule (v269.0, whole extension since v270.0): new or changed UI text — chat, panel, menus, dialogs, message boxes — is wrapped in `L("...")`/`N("...")`/`{local:Loc '...'}` and translated in every `lang/*.json` in the same change (recipe: `docs/SKILLS.md` → *Localize chat text*); `test.cmd` fails on a missing or orphaned translation. Text set from code must also be redone by `RefreshChatLanguage()` (or a tool window's own `Loc.LanguageChanged` handler) so a language switch reaches everything already open.
- Performance values rule (v279.0): the resumed-transcript limits and any other value chosen for performance (throttle intervals, virtualization cache, rendering caps) change only together with a measurement recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` (method, machine, before/after); `ReplayLimitsMatchTheMeasuredValues` pins the limits.

lastPrompt: For issue https://github.com/dliedke/ClaudeCodeExtension/issues/264  if git pull from extension has uncommited or conflicts with changes, what happens? is it supossed to fix all issues?

input.command: gh issue view 264 --comments 2>&1 | head -80
input.description: View GitHub issue 264 with comments

content.content:
author:	dliedke
association:	owner
edited:	false
status:	none
--
Thanks for the report and the screenshot!

**1. The automatic git pull**

This comes from the **"Pull from git before the first prompt"** setting (⚙ → Settings... → Automation → Git). It is on by default. Before the first prompt of a Visual Studio session it runs `git pull` in the solution's repository, so the agent doesn't start editing code that is already out of date on the remote. It runs once per solution per session, not on every message. Because you had fetched, your branch had incoming commits, so the pull brought them in. They conflicted with your local changes, and the extension then put the conflict instructions in front of your message, which is the text you saw.

If you prefer to pull yourself, uncheck that option and the extension won't run `git pull` again.

To get back to where you were before the pull:
- If a merge is still in progress (`git status` says "You have unmerged paths" / "All conflicts fixed but you are still merging"), `git merge --abort` returns the branch to its pre-pull state.
- Your uncommitted changes were stashed automatically before the pull. Check `git stash list` and restore the `autostash` entry with `git stash pop` if your edits aren't in the working tree anymore. Please don't drop that stash; it's the only copy of those edits.

**2. The `[200~` at the start and `[201~` at the end**

That isn't expected. The extension sends multi-line prompts to Claude Code as a single "bracketed paste", wrapped in invisible start/end markers. In your case the invisible part of the markers was lost on the way, so Claude Code showed them as text. It only happens with multi-line prompts, which is why you saw it here: the conflict instructions made your prompt several lines long.

To track this down, could you tell me:
- Your Windows version (Windows 10 or 11, and the build number from `winver`)
- Your Visual Studio version and the extension version
- The terminal type in ⚙ → Settings... (Command Prompt or Windows Terminal), and whether Native Mode is on or off
- Whether it also happens when you type a short prompt with a line break (Shift+Enter) in the prompt box, with no git conflict involved
- Whether "Disable clipboard" or "Send large prompts as file" is enabled in Settings

I'll leave this issue open for the marker problem.

--

449:## Pull Before Sending (GitSync.cs, v185.0)
450-
451-- Purpose: the agent should never start editing a file that is already out of date on the remote. `_settings.AutoGitPullBeforePrompt` (default **true**, Settings → Automation → Git) runs `git pull` in the workspace repository before a user-initiated prompt goes out
452-[Omitted long context line]
453-- The flag is set from `GitPullOutcome.PullExecuted` (true whenever the `pull` command itself ran, including when it *failed*) — an offline or unauthenticated remote would otherwise re-pay the full 20 s `GitSyncPullTimeoutMs` on every prompt for the rest of the session. Leftover conflicts found *before* any pull set `PullExecuted = false`, so the session's pull stays available for the next prompt
454-- The local `GetUnmergedPaths` check at the top of `RunAutoPull` still runs on **every** prompt, before the `allowNetworkPull` guard: it is a local `git status`, and a prompt going out over an unresolved tree is worth interrupting no matter who left it conflicted
455-[Omitted long context line]
456-[Omitted long context line]
457-- Progress line (v187.0): just before the network pull, `ShowAutoPullProgressAsync` starts the chat's spinner + running clock with the label "Pulling latest changes from git…" (native mode only, and only when a pull will actually run, i.e. the first prompt per repository); `HideAutoPullProgressAsync` clears it in a `finally`, and the turn's own `BeginActivity` takes over right after.
458-- Every git process runs on a background thread via `Task.Run(() => RunAutoPull(...))`; the handler switches back to the main thread before touching the control again
459-- Skip conditions (all silent, `GitPullOutcomeKind.Skipped`): setting off, no git repo, git not resolvable, no tracking branch (`rev-parse @{u}` fails — detached HEAD, local-only branch, no remote), or `IsNativeAgentBusy()`. The busy check matters for the providers that accept follow-ups mid-turn (Codex queues them, Devin steers with them): pulling mid-turn would rewrite files the agent is editing
460-- **Conflicts are not rolled back — they become the prompt.** `--no-rebase` is deliberate: a conflicted merge leaves conflict markers, a `git status` an agent can read, and `git merge --abort` as the escape hatch. A half-finished rebase is none of those things. On conflict, `BuildConflictPromptBlock` is prepended to `fullPrompt` ahead of the attachment block, listing the unmerged paths and telling the agent to resolve them before the user's own request
461-- **Two different conflict states, opposite instructions.** This is the single non-obvious thing in the file. Measured with git 2.55.0.windows.5 on scratch repos:
462-
463-  | Situation | Exit | `MERGE_HEAD` | `MERGE_AUTOSTASH` | `git stash list` |
464-  |---|---|---|---|---|
465-  | Local commit diverged + conflicting upstream | 1 | present | present | empty |
466-  | Clean-ish tree, only *uncommitted* edits conflict with upstream | **0** | **absent** | absent | `stash@{0}: autostash` |
467-
468-[Omitted long context line]
469-- Because of that exit-0 case, **unmerged paths — not the exit code — decide the outcome**: `RunAutoPull` re-reads `GetUnmergedPaths` after the pull and short-circuits to `BuildConflictOutcome` before it ever looks at whether HEAD moved, and `ClassifyPullResult` checks conflicts first in both directions
470-- `--autostash` lets the pull run with uncommitted work in the tree instead of git refusing outright. Merge-pull `--autostash` needs git 2.27+; `MentionsUnsupportedAutoStash` detects an older git rejecting the option and retries the plain `pull --no-rebase`
471-- Leftover conflicts from a previous turn short-circuit the whole thing before any pull: `RunAutoPull` checks `GetUnmergedPaths` first and re-sends the conflict block (with a "still open" wording via the `pulled: false` flag), so a second prompt can't stack a new pull on an unresolved tree
472-- `RunGitDetailed` is a separate runner from Diff.cs's `RunGitCommand` (which returns null and drops stderr on any non-zero exit — that is exactly what distinguishes a conflicted pull from an unreachable remote). It sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GCM_INTERACTIVE=never` so a credential prompt fails fast instead of hanging behind an invisible dialog for the full 20 s `GitSyncPullTimeoutMs`
473-- "Updated" vs "up to date" is decided by comparing `rev-parse HEAD` before and after, not by scraping git's output (localized, and "Already up to date." wording has changed across versions). An up-to-date pull produces **no** notice — it is the common case and a notice on every prompt would be noise. Updated / conflicted / failed pulls post a `ChatMessageKind.Notice` through `ReportAutoPullOutcome`, native mode only (terminal mode has nowhere to put one) and always to `Debug.WriteLine`
474-- Pure helpers (`ParseUnmergedPaths`, `ClassifyPullResult`, `MentionsUnsupportedAutoStash`, `StashListMentionsAutoStash`, `BuildConflictPromptBlock`) are `public static` and covered by `Tests/GitSyncTests.cs`, including a regression test asserting the no-merge branch never says "complete the merge"

476-## Pending Review (PendingReview.cs, Diff/PendingReviewTracker.cs, Diff/GitPendingReviewSource.cs, #183, v218.0)
477-
478-[Omitted long context line]
479-- **Snapshots are in memory only** and per repository: `GetOrCreatePendingReview` replaces the tracker when the workspace's repo root changes, so switching solutions drops the pending list. Closing VS loses it too
480-[Omitted long context line]
481-[Omitted long context line]
482-- **Overlapping turns**: `BeginTurn` reconciles against the old reference *before* taking the new one. Anything changed before the new snapshot is then already pending with its older baseline, and anything changed after it was untouched at snapshot time — so the new reference is safe to use for everyone. The reference is dropped only when the last open turn ends
483-- **Keep / Undo while a turn is running**: `Keep` writes the file's current bytes and `MarkUndone` the restored bytes into the live reference, otherwise the running turn's next reconcile would put the file straight back on the list
484-- **Ordering**: all tracker work runs on one background `Task` chain (`RunPendingReviewWorkAsync`). An end queued just before the next prompt's begin (same session key) must not run after it — that would close the new turn and lose its reference. `BeginPendingReviewTurnAsync` is *awaited* before the prompt is sent; `EndPendingReviewTurn` is fire-and-forget (the turn's completion path must not wait on git) and then refreshes the view
485-- **Hooks**: Begin — both `SendSinglePromptToNativeAgentAsync` overloads (right before `SendAsync`, after `TurnInFlight` is set), the terminal branch of `SendTextToAgentAsync`, `SendButton_Click` terminal path, and the terminal Enter hook in Terminal.cs (when the completion watcher isn't already armed). End — `CompleteNativeTurn` / `CompleteNativeTurnForSession`, the native send catch blocks, and the On Agent Finish idle detection for the terminal
486-- **Dead turns**: a chat tab closed mid-turn or an agent relaunched never reports the turn's end. Each Begin first ends every other open key that `CapturePendingReviewDeadTurns` doesn't find alive (terminal key always alive; native keys alive only while their session has a turn in flight)
487-- **Terminal limits**: without On Agent Finish idle detection the terminal turn stays open until the next prompt (still correct, just a wider window). A typed Enter in the terminal snapshots slightly *after* the prompt reached the CLI — it still lands well before a typical first edit. And while any turn is open, the user's own edits are indistinguishable from the agent's
488-[Omitted long context line]
489-- **Undo** restores the baseline bytes (`RestoreFileContent`) or deletes a file the agent created; deleted files are recreated, including their directory. Single Undo and Undo All both confirm first; Keep never does

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000ms / 30 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. That field belongs to diff tracking and is only ever assigned by `EnsureDiffTrackingStartedAsync`, which on the send path runs *after* the pull hook — null on the first prompt of a session, and after opening another solution in the same VS it still names the *previous* solution's repository. content.text:
Short answer: no. It doesn't promise to fix everything. If the pull conflicts, the extension leaves the conflict in place and puts instructions in front of your message so the agent resolves it before doing what you asked. Whether that works depends on the agent.

## What happens, case by case

The setting is "Pull from git before the first prompt" (Automation → Git, on by default). It runs `git pull --no-rebase --autostash` once per repository per VS session, before the first prompt you send yourself. The logic is in `Controls/ClaudeCodeControl.GitSync.cs`.

| Situation | What git does | What the extension does |
|---|---|---|
| Uncommitted edits, no overlap with incoming commits | Stashes the edits, merges, puts the edits back | In native mode it shows "Pulled the latest changes…". Your prompt goes out unchanged. |
| Uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes (likely what happened in #264) | The merge succeeds, but putting the stash back conflicts. Git exits 0 and is **not** mid-merge. The edits are left as conflict markers, and a copy stays in `git stash list` as `autostash`. | Adds a block before your prompt: list the files, resolve them keeping both sides, **don't commit, don't merge-commit, never `reset --hard` / `checkout --`**, drop the autostash only after the work is back in the files. |
| Local commits diverge from upstream and conflict | A real merge is left unfinished (`MERGE_HEAD` exists) | Adds a block before your prompt: resolve, stage, commit to finish the merge, never `merge --abort`, and make sure the autostash got restored. |
| Pull fails without conflicts (offline, auth, untracked files that would be overwritten, etc.) | Nothing changes | In native mode it shows "Auto-pull skipped: …". The prompt goes out unchanged. |
| Conflicts already exist before the pull | No pull runs | Sends the conflict block again on **every** prompt (with "still open" wording) until the tree is clean. |

## Is the agent supposed to fix it?

It's asked to, not guaranteed to. The block tells the agent to read both sides, keep the intent of each, and stop and ask when a conflict is ambiguous. The extension never rolls anything back on its own. The way out is always available: `git merge --abort` for the merge case, or the `autostash` entry for the uncommitted-edits case.

## Gaps this issue shows

1. **Terminal mode gives no notice.** The notices above appear only in native mode. In terminal mode, which the reporter used (the `[200~` markers mean bracketed paste in a terminal), a multi-line git block simply appears in their prompt with nothing explaining it. That's why it looked like text appeared from nowhere.
2. **Pulling just because you fetched is surprising.** Incoming commits after a fetch are exactly when the pull runs. Some users won't expect a "send message" button to change their branch.
3. **The `[200~`/`[201~` markers** are a separate bug in the bracketed-paste path. It only shows up because the conflict block made the prompt multi-line.

If you want, I can tackle 1 and/or 2. For example: show a short note in terminal mode as well, or switch the default from pulling to detect-and-warn.

s = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()

def rep(old, new):
    global s
    if old not in s:
        raise SystemExit("anchor not found: " + old[:80])
    s = s.replace(old, new, 1)

rep(''' *          never edits a file that is already out of date on the remote. A pull that ends in
 *          conflicts is not rolled back: the conflicted files are described in a block prepended to
 *          the prompt, so the agent resolves them as the first part of the turn.''',
''' *          never edits a file that is already out of date on the remote. The pull fetches first and
 *          is held back (nothing merged, a notice instead) when the incoming commits touch files the
 *          user has edited locally or would conflict with local commits (#264). Conflicts that
 *          still happen, or were already open, are described in a block prepended to the prompt,
 *          so the agent resolves them as the first part of the turn.''')

rep('''        /// <summary>The pull left conflicted files in the working tree.</summary>
        Conflicts,''', '''        /// <summary>The pull left conflicted files in the working tree.</summary>
        Conflicts,

        /// <summary>
        /// Incoming commits were found but not merged: they touch files with uncommitted local edits,
        /// or would conflict with local commits. Nothing in the working tree was changed.
        /// </summary>
        HeldBack,''')

old_start = s.index('            string upstreamName = upstream.StdOut.Trim();\n            string headBefore')
old_end = s.index('        /// <summary>\n        /// Reads the repository state that decides')
new = open(sys.argv[2], encoding='utf-8').read()
s = s[:old_start] + new + s[old_end:]

anchor = '        /// <summary>True when `git stash list` output contains an autostash entry.</summary>'
helpers = open(sys.argv[3], encoding='utf-8').read()
rep(anchor, helpers + anchor)

rep('''                || stdErr.IndexOf("usage: git pull", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) >= 0;''',
'''                || stdErr.IndexOf("usage: git pull", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) >= 0
                || stdErr.IndexOf("usage: git merge", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) >= 0;''')
open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)
print("ok")

content.content:
449	## Pull Before Sending (GitSync.cs, v185.0)
450	
451	- Purpose: the agent should never start editing a file that is already out of date on the remote. `_settings.AutoGitPullBeforePrompt` (default **true**, Settings → Automation → Git) runs `git pull` in the workspace repository before a user-initiated prompt goes out
452	- **Once per repository per session, not per prompt.** `_autoPulledRepositoryRoot` remembers the repo the pull ran for; `RunAutoPull` takes an `allowNetworkPull` flag and returns early when it is false. Rationale: by the second prompt the working tree normally holds the agent's *own* uncommitted edits, so a pull then is both the most likely to produce an autostash-restore conflict (see below) and the least likely to find anything — while charging every single send a network round-trip on the UI path. Keyed by root rather than a bare bool so switching solutions re-arms it; it does **not** re-arm on agent restart or after an idle period
453	- The flag is set from `GitPullOutcome.PullExecuted` (true whenever the `pull` command itself ran, including when it *failed*) — an offline or unauthenticated remote would otherwise re-pay the full 20 s `GitSyncPullTimeoutMs` on every prompt for the rest of the session. Leftover conflicts found *before* any pull set `PullExecuted = false`, so the session's pull stays available for the next prompt
454	- The local `GetUnmergedPaths` check at the top of `RunAutoPull` still runs on **every** prompt, before the `allowNetworkPull` guard: it is a local `git status`, and a prompt going out over an unresolved tree is worth interrupting no matter who left it conflicted
455	- Repository resolution **never** reads `_gitRepositoryRoot` (v234.0): `TryAutoPullBeforePromptAsync` always resolves `GetWorkspaceDirectoryAsync()` + `FindGitRepositoryRoot()` (a local walk up for `.git`). That field belongs to diff tracking and is only ever assigned by `EnsureDiffTrackingStartedAsync`, which on the send path runs *after* the pull hook — null on the first prompt of a session, and after opening another solution in the same VS it still names the *previous* solution's repository. ## Pull Before Sending (GitSync.cs, v185.0)

- Purpose: the agent should never start editing a file that is already out of date on the remote. `_settings.AutoGitPullBeforePrompt` (default **true**, Settings → Automation → Git) runs `git pull` in the workspace repository before a user-initiated prompt goes out
- **Once per repository per session, not per prompt.** `_autoPulledRepositoryRoot` remembers the repo the pull ran for; `RunAutoPull` takes an `allowNetworkPull` flag and returns early when it is false. Rationale: by the second prompt the working tree normally holds the agent's *own* uncommitted edits, so a pull then is both the most likely to produce an autostash-restore conflict (see below) and the least likely to find anything — while charging every single send a network round-trip on the UI path. Keyed by root rather than a bare bool so switching solutions re-arms it; it does **not** re-arm on agent restart or after an idle period
- The flag is set from `GitPullOutcome.PullExecuted` (true whenever the `pull` command itself ran, including when it *failed*) — an offline or unauthenticated remote would otherwise re-pay the full 20 s `GitSyncPullTimeoutMs` on every prompt for the rest of the session. Leftover conflicts found *before* any pull set `PullExecuted = false`, so the session's pull stays available for the next prompt
- The local `GetUnmergedPaths` check at the top of `RunAutoPull` still runs on **every** prompt, before the `allowNetworkPull` guard: it is a local `git status`, and a prompt going out over an unresolved tree is worth interrupting no matter who left it conflicted
- Repository resolution **never** reads `_gitRepositoryRoot` (v234.0): `TryAutoPullBeforePromptAsync` always resolves `GetWorkspaceDirectoryAsync()` + `FindGitRepositoryRoot()` (a local walk up for `.git`). That field belongs to diff tracking and is only ever assigned by `EnsureDiffTrackingStartedAsync`, which on the send path runs *after* the pull hook — null on the first prompt of a session, and after opening another solution in the same VS it still names the *previous* solution's repository. Before v234.0 the pull used it when non-empty, so the new solution's first prompt resolved the old root, found it already in `_autoPulledRepositoryRoot`, and went out unpulled (measured: one VS process, Devin native in `GOT` then `GenesysAutomations`). Every skip path goes through `LogSkip`, which writes to `Debug.WriteLine` **and** `terminal-launch.log` (Debug output is compiled out of Release, and a skip is silent by design); `ReportAutoPullOutcome` logs the outcome there too. The "already pulled" skip names the repository root, so a stale root shows up in the log
- Hooked into `SendButton_Click` (UserInput.cs) and, since v193.0, `CustomCommandMenuItem_Click` (CustomCommands.cs) — both are user-initiated sends. Deliberately *not* into `SendTextToAgentAsync` itself: the automatic senders (build errors, runtime errors, agent-finish follow-ups) must not trigger network I/O or move files under a turn that is already running, so they call `SendTextToAgentAsync` directly without going through either hook. In `SendButton_Click` it sits after `_isSendingPrompt = true` (so the pull's await can't let a second Enter through) and before `EnsureDiffTrackingStartedAsync(false)` (so pulled files land in the diff baseline instead of showing up as the agent's own changes). Before v193.0 a custom command as the *first* send of a session skipped the pull entirely — `TryAutoPullBeforePromptAsync` only ever ran from `SendButton_Click` — so `CustomCommandMenuItem_Click` now runs the same pull + conflict-block-prepend before calling `SendTextToAgentAsync`
- Progress line (v187.0): just before the network pull, `ShowAutoPullProgressAsync` starts the chat's spinner + running clock with the label "Pulling latest changes from git…" (native mode only, and only when a pull will actually run, i.e. the first prompt per repository); `HideAutoPullProgressAsync` clears it in a `finally`, and the turn's own `BeginActivity` takes over right after.
- Every git process runs on a background thread via `Task.Run(() => RunAutoPull(...))`; the handler switches back to the main thread before touching the control again
- Skip conditions (all silent, `GitPullOutcomeKind.Skipped`): setting off, no git repo, git not resolvable, no tracking branch (`rev-parse @{u}` fails — detached HEAD, local-only branch, no remote), or `IsNativeAgentBusy()`.
