650:- "Pull from git before the first prompt" now also fires when the first message of a session is sent from a custom command, not just when typed into the prompt box.
199:## Version History
33:- TUI fullscreen env vars (v31/v32, `GetClaudeCommand`): `_settings.ClaudeTuiFullscreen` (nullable) injects an env prefix ahead of the `claude` command — `true` → `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1` plus `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE=1`; `false` → `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN=1` (classic renderer); `null` → nothing (CLI default). cmd.exe form is `set X=1 && set Y=1 && {cmd}`, WSL bash form is `X=1 Y=1 {cmd}`. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE` is mandatory whenever fullscreen is on (issue #92): fullscreen rendering enables Claude Code's own terminal mouse tracking, which in the embedded conhost — where the extension already runs a global mouse hook and re-asserts focus — emits a continuous burst of mouse-input escape sequences that Claude's fast-input heuristic collapses into `[Pasted text +N lines]` bracketed-paste blocks, flooding the prompt on launch and on every restart. The extension supplies its own mouse zoom / click-to-focus / paste, so disabling Claude's mouse capture loses nothing while keeping the flicker-free draw. The one casualty is wheel scrolling: with Claude's mouse off, the wheel no longer pages the conversation (per Claude's docs, fullscreen + `DISABLE_MOUSE` keeps only the keyboard scroll keys `PgUp`/`PgDn`/`Ctrl+Home`/`Ctrl+End`, plus native terminal selection of the visible viewport). Wheel scroll restored without re-enabling Claude's mouse (v36, issue #96): the global mouse hook's `HandleMouseHookEvent` now, on a plain (no-Ctrl) wheel notch over the active panel when `IsClaudeFullscreenConhostActive()`, posts `VK_PRIOR`/`VK_NEXT` (PgUp/PgDn) keystrokes to the terminal via `SendScrollKeyToTerminal`. Two gotchas: (1) `ShouldDispatchMouseHookMessage` must let the plain wheel through — it otherwise forwards `WM_MOUSEWHEEL` only when Ctrl is held (zoom), so the plain-wheel case is gated on `IsClaudeFullscreenConhostActive()` there too, or the handler never runs. (2) `SendScrollKeyToTerminal` builds a real `lParam` (scan code from `MapVirtualKey` + extended-key bit) — conhost silently drops a posted key with a zero scan code instead of translating it to VT input (`ESC[5~`/`ESC[6~`). Posted straight to `terminalHandle` (focus-independent, like the Enter path); gated to conhost (`_wtTabBarHeight <= 0`) and the Claude Code / Claude Code (WSL) providers so it never hijacks conhost's own scrollback in the classic renderer or Windows Terminal's native wheel handling. Smooth line scroll (vs. the half-page PgUp default): for *native* Claude Code, `TryEnsureFullscreenLineScrollKeybinding()` merges `pageup`→`scroll:lineUp`, `pagedown`→`scroll:lineDown` (and `shift+pageup/pagedown`→`scroll:halfPage*` to preserve paging) into `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\keybindings.json` — those line-scroll actions are unbound by default, so the wheel had nothing finer than half-page to trigger. With the binding in place each notch sends one PgUp/PgDn (`GetFullscreenWheelScrollKeystrokeCount()` returns 1) for a one-line step; WSL Claude (config lives in the WSL filesystem) and any write failure fall back to a single half-page keystroke. The keybinding file is touched once per session, lazily on first wheel scroll, and merges without overwriting existing user bindings (`AddBindingIfAbsent`).
259:- Legacy Windows 10 console host (v72.0, #83): `IsLegacyWindows10Console()` (TerminalIO.cs) reads `CurrentBuildNumber` from the registry — not `Environment.OSVersion`, which the host manifest can shim — and caches it; `< 22000` = Windows 10. That host has no bracketed-paste support, so a paste reaches a TUI as ordinary keystrokes. Under it, UserInput.cs (a) forces prompts over the 1 KB threshold onto the temp-file reference regardless of `SendLargePromptsAsFile`, and (b) disables the `DisableClipboardSend` keystroke path so sends stay on the single handle-targeted `WM_COMMAND` paste
265:- Mouse pointer restore after send (v110.0, issue #122): Windows' "Hide pointer while typing" (`SPI_SETMOUSEVANISH`, on by default) hides the cursor with `SetCursor(NULL)` on each keystroke and normally restores it on the next mouse move, when the window under the pointer handles `WM_SETCURSOR`. That restore does not arrive here: `SetParent` permanently joins the embedded terminal thread's input queue with the VS UI thread (see issue #65), so both share one pointer-visibility state, and while an agent streams output the terminal thread can stop pumping long enough that the restoring `WM_SETCURSOR` is never processed — the pointer stays invisible until the user drifts over a VS window that is still pumping. Codex triggers it most because its TUI repaints continuously for the whole reply. Fix: `RestoreMousePointer()` (UserInput.cs, `#region Mouse Pointer Visibility`) calls `SetCursor` directly, bypassing `WM_SETCURSOR`, from `SendTextToTerminalAsync`'s `finally` (after every injected keystroke has been delivered) and at the end of `SendTextViaKeystrokesAsync`; `PromptTextBox_PreviewKeyDown` uses it too instead of its old inline `SetCursor`. The shape comes from `IsPointerOverTerminal()` — Win32-only (`GetCursorPos` + `GetWindowRect`, no WPF hit test, safe from any thread) — arrow over the terminal, I-beam elsewhere, so the correction is invisible; a real mouse move re-asserts the proper cursor through the normal path anyway. Do not try to re-assert the cursor from the low-level mouse hook on every `WM_MOUSEMOVE`: `ShouldDispatchMouseHookMessage` exists precisely to keep those high-frequency events off the dispatcher, and the hook thread is outside the relevant input queue
418:- Actions (`ExecuteMainActionAsync`, returns `bool` success): Build/Rebuild → `BuildAndCheckSuccessAsync()` (`dte.ExecuteCommand` + `WaitForDteBuildToFinishAsync` + `SolutionBuild.LastBuildInfo` — false on timeout or a failed project); Run/RunWithoutDebugging → `PrepareAndRunAsync()` (also returns `bool`: false if the clean/rebuild gate failed or timed out, otherwise true after issuing `Debug.Start`/`Debug.StartWithoutDebugging`); RunTests → `dte.ExecuteCommand("TestExplorer.RunAllTests")` (fire-and-forget, always true — no completion signal available); RunScript → `RunFinishScriptAsync` `Process.Start` (`UseShellExecute`) in the workspace dir, always true (fire-and-forget) — a `.cmd`/`.bat` is wrapped as `cmd.exe /k "<path>"` and a `.ps1` as `powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoExit -File "<path>"` (the `.ps1` default shell verb is Edit, so shell-executing it directly would open an editor; `/k`/`-NoExit` keep the console open for output), anything else is shell-executed directly; SendToAgent → `SendTextToAgentAsync` (terminal paste, or the structured channel under native mode — see *Native Mode*), always true. `RequireFileChanges` gates on `git status --porcelain` in `_gitRepositoryRoot` (non-git ⇒ never blocks); the change check runs before the chime/info-bar in `OnAgentTurnCompletedAsync`, so when the action is skipped for lack of changes the turn is fully silent (no sound, no notification) rather than announcing the skip. `Confirm` (default true) surfaces the action as an info-bar button instead of auto-running
436:- Large-prompt delivery (v68.0): both send paths go through `SendBuildErrorPromptAsync` rather than calling `SendTextToTerminalAsync` directly. A handful of errors with full relative paths easily clears ~1 KB, and a raw clipboard paste that large risked leaving the CLI's bracketed-paste state stuck mid-transfer (terminal shows "Pasting..." forever, nothing arrives) — the same failure mode `SendLargePromptsAsFile` exists to avoid for the prompt box (`LargePromptThresholdChars` in UserInput.cs). Since this text is generated, not typed, `SendBuildErrorPromptAsync` applies the file-reference trick unconditionally above `LargeBuildErrorPromptThresholdChars` (1024 chars, same threshold) regardless of the user's `SendLargePromptsAsFile` toggle: writes the prompt to a temp `.md` under `%TEMP%\ClaudeCodeVS_Session\<guid>\`, WSL-path-converts it for WSL providers, and sends `"Read and follow: <path>"` instead of the raw text
536:- Trigger: `PromptTextBox`'s `TextChanged` (wired in XAML) and `ComposerInputBox`'s `TextChanged` (subscribed in code from `WireChatComposer`, NativeChat.cs) both call `UpdateAtMentionPopup(target)`, which detects an `@` token under the caret (`@` at text start or after whitespace, followed by non-whitespace). On by default; `_settings.AtMentionEnabled` false (Settings → Prompt → "Show the @ file picker", v276.0) hides it and skips indexing entirely — checked after `TryUpdateSlashPopup`, so the "/" picker is unaffected
577:Alternative to the embedded terminal: the panel renders the conversation as a WPF chat and talks to the CLI over its headless JSON protocol instead of screen-scraping a console. Gated by `_settings.UseNativeMode` (single global bool, default true since v179.0 — new installs with no settings file land in native mode; upgrades keep whatever was already saved, since `LoadSettings` only applies the class default when no settings file exists. Settings → Terminal tab); changing it restarts the agent like a terminal-type change.
716:- Bare URLs and file citations are auto-linked too (v107.0), not just `[label](url)` syntax — measured against a real turn, agents asked for `file.cs:41`-style citations wrote plain text with no brackets around it far more often than markdown links. `AppendInlines` matches `AutoUrlPattern` (`https?://…`, trimmed of trailing sentence punctuation via `TrimTrailingPunctuation`) and `AutoFileRefPattern` (`path/File.ext:123` or `:123-456`, requiring a dot-plus-extension before the colon so "ratio 3:1" or a "10:41" timestamp is never mistaken for a citation) at every `h`/word-start character, and routes a hit through the same `BuildLink` as an explicit link. Bracketed links are matched first (the `[` branch runs before the autolink checks) so nothing double-processes.

199:## Version History
33:- TUI fullscreen env vars (v31/v32, `GetClaudeCommand`): `_settings.ClaudeTuiFullscreen` (nullable) injects an env prefix ahead of the `claude` command — `true` → `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1` plus `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE=1`; `false` → `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN=1` (classic renderer); `null` → nothing (CLI default). cmd.exe form is `set X=1 && set Y=1 && {cmd}`, WSL bash form is `X=1 Y=1 {cmd}`. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE` is mandatory whenever fullscreen is on (issue #92): fullscreen rendering enables Claude Code's own terminal mouse tracking, which in the embedded conhost — where the extension already runs a global mouse hook and re-asserts focus — emits a continuous burst of mouse-input escape sequences that Claude's fast-input heuristic collapses into `[Pasted text +N lines]` bracketed-paste blocks, flooding the prompt on launch and on every restart. The extension supplies its own mouse zoom / click-to-focus / paste, so disabling Claude's mouse capture loses nothing while keeping the flicker-free draw. The one casualty is wheel scrolling: with Claude's mouse off, the wheel no longer pages the conversation (per Claude's docs, fullscreen + `DISABLE_MOUSE` keeps only the keyboard scroll keys `PgUp`/`PgDn`/`Ctrl+Home`/`Ctrl+End`, plus native terminal selection of the visible viewport). Wheel scroll restored without re-enabling Claude's mouse (v36, issue #96): the global mouse hook's `HandleMouseHookEvent` now, on a plain (no-Ctrl) wheel notch over the active panel when `IsClaudeFullscreenConhostActive()`, posts `VK_PRIOR`/`VK_NEXT` (PgUp/PgDn) keystrokes to the terminal via `SendScrollKeyToTerminal`. Two gotchas: (1) `ShouldDispatchMouseHookMessage` must let the plain wheel through — it otherwise forwards `WM_MOUSEWHEEL` only when Ctrl is held (zoom), so the plain-wheel case is gated on `IsClaudeFullscreenConhostActive()` there too, or the handler never runs. (2) `SendScrollKeyToTerminal` builds a real `lParam` (scan code from `MapVirtualKey` + extended-key bit) — conhost silently drops a posted key with a zero scan code instead of translating it to VT input (`ESC[5~`/`ESC[6~`). Posted straight to `terminalHandle` (focus-independent, like the Enter path); gated to conhost (`_wtTabBarHeight <= 0`) and the Claude Code / Claude Code (WSL) providers so it never hijacks conhost's own scrollback in the classic renderer or Windows Terminal's native wheel handling. Smooth line scroll (vs. the half-page PgUp default): for *native* Claude Code, `TryEnsureFullscreenLineScrollKeybinding()` merges `pageup`→`scroll:lineUp`, `pagedown`→`scroll:lineDown` (and `shift+pageup/pagedown`→`scroll:halfPage*` to preserve paging) into `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\keybindings.json` — those line-scroll actions are unbound by default, so the wheel had nothing finer than half-page to trigger. With the binding in place each notch sends one PgUp/PgDn (`GetFullscreenWheelScrollKeystrokeCount()` returns 1) for a one-line step; WSL Claude (config lives in the WSL filesystem) and any write failure fall back to a single half-page keystroke. The keybinding file is touched once per session, lazily on first wheel scroll, and merges without overwriting existing user bindings (`AddBindingIfAbsent`).
259:- Legacy Windows 10 console host (v72.0, #83): `IsLegacyWindows10Console()` (TerminalIO.cs) reads `CurrentBuildNumber` from the registry — not `Environment.OSVersion`, which the host manifest can shim — and caches it; `< 22000` = Windows 10. That host has no bracketed-paste support, so a paste reaches a TUI as ordinary keystrokes. Under it, UserInput.cs (a) forces prompts over the 1 KB threshold onto the temp-file reference regardless of `SendLargePromptsAsFile`, and (b) disables the `DisableClipboardSend` keystroke path so sends stay on the single handle-targeted `WM_COMMAND` paste
265:- Mouse pointer restore after send (v110.0, issue #122): Windows' "Hide pointer while typing" (`SPI_SETMOUSEVANISH`, on by default) hides the cursor with `SetCursor(NULL)` on each keystroke and normally restores it on the next mouse move, when the window under the pointer handles `WM_SETCURSOR`. That restore does not arrive here: `SetParent` permanently joins the embedded terminal thread's input queue with the VS UI thread (see issue #65), so both share one pointer-visibility state, and while an agent streams output the terminal thread can stop pumping long enough that the restoring `WM_SETCURSOR` is never processed — the pointer stays invisible until the user drifts over a VS window that is still pumping. Codex triggers it most because its TUI repaints continuously for the whole reply. Fix: `RestoreMousePointer()` (UserInput.cs, `#region Mouse Pointer Visibility`) calls `SetCursor` directly, bypassing `WM_SETCURSOR`, from `SendTextToTerminalAsync`'s `finally` (after every injected keystroke has been delivered) and at the end of `SendTextViaKeystrokesAsync`; `PromptTextBox_PreviewKeyDown` uses it too instead of its old inline `SetCursor`. The shape comes from `IsPointerOverTerminal()` — Win32-only (`GetCursorPos` + `GetWindowRect`, no WPF hit test, safe from any thread) — arrow over the terminal, I-beam elsewhere, so the correction is invisible; a real mouse move re-asserts the proper cursor through the normal path anyway. Do not try to re-assert the cursor from the low-level mouse hook on every `WM_MOUSEMOVE`: `ShouldDispatchMouseHookMessage` exists precisely to keep those high-frequency events off the dispatcher, and the hook thread is outside the relevant input queue
418:- Actions (`ExecuteMainActionAsync`, returns `bool` success): Build/Rebuild → `BuildAndCheckSuccessAsync()` (`dte.ExecuteCommand` + `WaitForDteBuildToFinishAsync` + `SolutionBuild.LastBuildInfo` — false on timeout or a failed project); Run/RunWithoutDebugging → `PrepareAndRunAsync()` (also returns `bool`: false if the clean/rebuild gate failed or timed out, otherwise true after issuing `Debug.Start`/`Debug.StartWithoutDebugging`); RunTests → `dte.ExecuteCommand("TestExplorer.RunAllTests")` (fire-and-forget, always true — no completion signal available); RunScript → `RunFinishScriptAsync` `Process.Start` (`UseShellExecute`) in the workspace dir, always true (fire-and-forget) — a `.cmd`/`.bat` is wrapped as `cmd.exe /k "<path>"` and a `.ps1` as `powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoExit -File "<path>"` (the `.ps1` default shell verb is Edit, so shell-executing it directly would open an editor; `/k`/`-NoExit` keep the console open for output), anything else is shell-executed directly; SendToAgent → `SendTextToAgentAsync` (terminal paste, or the structured channel under native mode — see *Native Mode*), always true. `RequireFileChanges` gates on `git status --porcelain` in `_gitRepositoryRoot` (non-git ⇒ never blocks); the change check runs before the chime/info-bar in `OnAgentTurnCompletedAsync`, so when the action is skipped for lack of changes the turn is fully silent (no sound, no notification) rather than announcing the skip. `Confirm` (default true) surfaces the action as an info-bar button instead of auto-running
436:- Large-prompt delivery (v68.0): both send paths go through `SendBuildErrorPromptAsync` rather than calling `SendTextToTerminalAsync` directly. A handful of errors with full relative paths easily clears ~1 KB, and a raw clipboard paste that large risked leaving the CLI's bracketed-paste state stuck mid-transfer (terminal shows "Pasting..." forever, nothing arrives) — the same failure mode `SendLargePromptsAsFile` exists to avoid for the prompt box (`LargePromptThresholdChars` in UserInput.cs). Since this text is generated, not typed, `SendBuildErrorPromptAsync` applies the file-reference trick unconditionally above `LargeBuildErrorPromptThresholdChars` (1024 chars, same threshold) regardless of the user's `SendLargePromptsAsFile` toggle: writes the prompt to a temp `.md` under `%TEMP%\ClaudeCodeVS_Session\<guid>\`, WSL-path-converts it for WSL providers, and sends `"Read and follow: <path>"` instead of the raw text
536:- Trigger: `PromptTextBox`'s `TextChanged` (wired in XAML) and `ComposerInputBox`'s `TextChanged` (subscribed in code from `WireChatComposer`, NativeChat.cs) both call `UpdateAtMentionPopup(target)`, which detects an `@` token under the caret (`@` at text start or after whitespace, followed by non-whitespace). On by default; `_settings.AtMentionEnabled` false (Settings → Prompt → "Show the @ file picker", v276.0) hides it and skips indexing entirely — checked after `TryUpdateSlashPopup`, so the "/" picker is unaffected
577:Alternative to the embedded terminal: the panel renders the conversation as a WPF chat and talks to the CLI over its headless JSON protocol instead of screen-scraping a console. Gated by `_settings.UseNativeMode` (single global bool, default true since v179.0 — new installs with no settings file land in native mode; upgrades keep whatever was already saved, since `LoadSettings` only applies the class default when no settings file exists. Settings → Terminal tab); changing it restarts the agent like a terminal-type change.
716:- Bare URLs and file citations are auto-linked too (v107.0), not just `[label](url)` syntax — measured against a real turn, agents asked for `file.cs:41`-style citations wrote plain text with no brackets around it far more often than markdown links. `AppendInlines` matches `AutoUrlPattern` (`https?://…`, trimmed of trailing sentence punctuation via `TrimTrailingPunctuation`) and `AutoFileRefPattern` (`path/File.ext:123` or `:123-456`, requiring a dot-plus-extension before the colon so "ratio 3:1" or a "10:41" timestamp is never mistaken for a citation) at every `h`/word-start character, and routes a hit through the same `BuildLink` as an explicit link. Bracketed links are matched first (the `[` branch runs before the autolink checks) so nothing double-processes.

- Mouse-mode probe is tri-state (v72.0, #83): `IsTerminalInMouseInputMode()` returns `bool?` — `null` means the console attach / `GetConsoleMode` failed, which is not the same as "QuickEdit is on". `SendTextToTerminalAsync` treats `null` as "mouse captured" and skips the deselect right-click. Reporting unknown as `false` injected a real right-click into a TUI owning the mouse; each synthetic mouse event came back as a mouse-report escape sequence on the agent's stdin, which the CLI rendered as a runaway series of `[Pasted text #N]` blocks (only reproducible on Windows 10). - Legacy Windows 10 console host (v72.0, #83): `IsLegacyWindows10Console()` (TerminalIO.cs) reads `CurrentBuildNumber` from the registry — not `Environment.OSVersion`, which the host manifest can shim — and caches it; `< 22000` = Windows 10. That host has no bracketed-paste support, so a paste reaches a TUI as ordinary keystrokes. Under it, UserInput.cs (a) forces prompts over the 1 KB threshold onto the temp-file reference regardless of `SendLargePromptsAsFile`, and (b) disables the `DisableClipboardSend` keystroke path so sends stay on the single handle-targeted `WM_COMMAND` paste

+- Purpose: the agent should never start editing a file that is already out of date on the remote. `_settings.AutoGitPullBeforePrompt` (default **false** since v309.0, #264 — an unexpected pull surprised users who merge coworkers' changes by hand; Settings → Automation → Git) runs `git pull` in the workspace repository before a user-initiated prompt goes out

- **Once per repository per session, not per prompt.** `_autoPulledRepositoryRoot` remembers the repo the pull ran for; `RunAutoPull` takes an `allowNetworkPull` flag and returns early when it is false. Rationale: by the second prompt the working tree normally holds the agent's *own* uncommitted edits, so a pull then is both the most likely to produce an autostash-restore conflict (see below) and the least likely to find anything — while charging every single send a network round-trip on the UI path. Keyed by root rather than a bare bool so switching solutions re-arms it; it does **not** re-arm on agent restart or after an idle period

- The flag is set from `GitPullOutcome.PullExecuted` (true whenever the `pull` command itself ran, including when it *failed*) — an offline or unauthenticated remote would otherwise re-pay the full 20 s `GitSyncPullTimeoutMs` on every prompt for the rest of the session. Leftover conflicts found *before* any pull set `PullExecuted = false`, so the session's pull stays available for the next prompt

- The local `GetUnmergedPaths` check at the top of `RunAutoPull` still runs on **every** prompt, before the `allowNetworkPull` guard: it is a local `git status`, and a prompt going out over an unresolved tree is worth interrupting no matter who left it conflicted

`AgentFinishConfig` defaults: `Enabled` false; `PlaySound`, `ShowToast` and `Confirm` true; `PlayQuestionSound` false (a distinct tone when the agent stops to wait for an answer); `IdleSeconds` 5 (forced to 1 in native mode); `AutoCloseScript` false (closes the `RunScript` window when the script ends); `CleanBeforeRun` and `RebuildBeforeRun` true (prepare the solution before `Run`/`RunWithoutDebugging`); `RequireFileChanges` false. The `FollowUp*` fields chain one step after the action: literal text, or one of the two commit-message presets (mutually exclusive) — see *On Agent Finish*.

-Key settings: `SplitterPosition` (236px default), `SendWithEnter` (default true), `SendWithCtrlEnter` (default false — when true and `SendWithEnter` false, Ctrl+Enter sends and Enter inserts a newline; issue #70), `SendSelectionReferenceOnly` (default false — Settings → Prompt; "Send Selection" inserts only the file path and line numbers, no code), `DisableClipboardSend` (default false — never paste: the prompt goes to a temp file and a short reference is typed with `SendInput`; Command Prompt only; issue #61), `SelectedProvider`, `VisibleProviders` (defaults to `[ClaudeCode]` — controls which agents appear in the provider menu; active provider is always shown regardless), `VisibleToolbarButtons` (`List<ToolbarButton>`, default `[RestartAgent, SessionHistory]` since v280.0 — features promoted to one-click toolbar buttons, the rest stay in ☰ Tools; see *Configurable Toolbar Buttons*), `ShowToolsMenuButton` (default true, v280.0 — Settings → Toolbar; hidden, unpromoted features are unreachable), `SessionHistoryButtonMigrated` (one-time flag, v280.0 — Session History promoted once when the composer's 🕘 merged into it), `ToolbarButtonOrder` (`List<ToolbarButton>`, default empty — the user's order for the toolbar and ☰ Tools (since v280.0 it also places ☰ ⚡ ⚙); `GetEffectiveToolbarOrder` completes empty/partial lists with the default order), `ToolbarButtonsRightAligned` (default false — Settings → Terminal since v291.0 (was Toolbar), under the prompt panel position; a strip narrower than its row sits at the right edge, the pre-v177 look; panel toolbar only — the chat tab's composer does not read it. Since v291.0 both ◀/▶ arrow slots collapse while nothing scrolls, so the strip sits flush against its aligned edge; the left slot used to stay Hidden and read as a gap before the first button), `SelectedClaudeModel`, `SelectedDevinModel` (string — the chosen Devin `model_uid`, shared by Devin (WSL) and Devin (native); empty = Devin's own default), `FavoriteDevinModels` (`List<string>` — Devin models starred as favorites, most recently starred first, uncapped; feeds the model menu's shortcuts and the picker's "Favorites"; v168.0, replaced the automatic `RecentDevinModels` MRU list), `SelectedProviderModels` (`Dictionary<string,string>` keyed by `AiProvider.ToString()` — the chosen model for every other agent; empty value = the agent's default) and `ModelCatalogs` (`Dictionary<string,ModelCatalogCache>` — the lists read from each CLI, 24h TTL; Reporting unknown as `false` injected a real right-click into a TUI owning the mouse; each synthetic mouse event came back as a mouse-report escape sequence on the agent's stdin, which the CLI rendered as a runaway series of `[Pasted text #N]` blocks (only reproducible on Windows 10).
